messages.subject: subsetting capture history
parts: Can we subset capture histories using a polygon or using different mask.? I would like to subset the capture histories using smaller polygon or mask

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: subsetting capture history
parts:
Hi Ujjwal
I think it would help to know more about your problem and why you want to do this. In general, I don't remember coding exactly what you ask for (spatial subset operation for polygon data), and it might be a little tricky. You could achieve the same result by first discretizing the polygon capthist (see ?discretize) and then subsetting using the traps argument (see ?subset.capthist), applying a criterion for whether each notional discretized trap was inside your desired area (see rough example code below). Masks are a different concept and probably not useful.
discreteCH <- discretize(polyCH, spacing = 500)  # choose spacing for your animal
newCH <- subset(discreteCH, traps = pointsInPolygon(traps(discreteCH), newpoly))
Regards
Murray

messages.subject: Re: subsetting capture history
parts:
Hi Murray
I have sampled with increasing sampling intensity and area in subsequent years e.g. 2010= 250 sqkm 2011 = 300 sqkm , 2012= 500 sqkm 2013 = 600 sqkm 2014 =700 sqkm, My sampling scale had changed in subsequent years due to logistic gain. I would like to compare the estimates (mostly Population) with the smallest sampling area that is 250 sqkm (what changes have occurred during subsequent years). Hence I would like to subset capture histories from the larger areas( eg 500sqkm area) to smallest sampling area 250 sqkm. I was curious if it is possible in secr.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: subsetting capture history
parts:
If density may be assumed homogeneous, I think you can achieve what you want just by comparing density across years, or by computing population size in a fixed region (the 'region' argument of region.N). No need to subset capture histories.
Murray
